title: Find a GitHub Profile: Search Syntax & Privacy Checks
description: Use GitHub user search, distinguish personal and organization profiles, and audit profile email separately from public commit email.
h1: Find a GitHub Profile: Search Syntax & Privacy Checks
intro: GitHub has separate personal and organization accounts, public repositories and profile fields. An exact handle URL is a useful starting point, but repository activity and a display name do not identify a person. This guide shows the GitHub search syntax and the fields worth checking in your own public profile.

sections.heading: Search a handle or restrict the account type
sections.body: Open https://github.com/HANDLE with the known handle, or use GitHub user search. The documented query user:octocat selects that username; octocat is GitHub's public example account. To restrict a broader search to personal accounts, add type:user. Use type:org for organizations. A query such as example in:login type:user searches username text; example in:name searches the displayed name. These fields answer different questions and a full-name result can contain many unrelated people.

sections.heading: Read the profile separately from repositories
sections.body: Confirm the final URL and whether it is a personal or organization page. Review the public biography, self-linked website and profile README. A repository owned by an organization is not proof that every contributor represents it. Forks are copies of repositories; their presence does not establish original authorship. Contribution graphs can include activity whose underlying repository is private, so a graph cannot reveal the private code or project contents.

sections.heading: Audit your email exposure
sections.body: In your own GitHub settings review public profile email and commit email separately. Hiding your profile email does not remove an address embedded in old public commits. GitHub documents a no-reply commit address and controls for blocking command-line pushes that expose your email. Apply those settings for future commits, then inspect the public commit information in repositories you control. Rewriting shared history requires coordination; do not promise that removing an address from one repository removes every clone.

sections.heading: Worked example and verification limits
sections.body: Reproduce the documented query user:octocat and compare its result with https://github.com/octocat. This is a provider-documented public example, not a claim that the account belongs to you. For a project account, a link from the official project website can support a public association. A same-name profile, similar avatar or repository star is weaker evidence. Record the final profile URL and observation date, and keep current control or legal identity outside the conclusion.

sections.heading: What the MyRecon check covers
sections.body: The standard release catalogue includes GitHub. Its username check supplies a public profile lead, not repository secret scanning, private repository access or an audit of every commit. MyRecon checks a catalogue of 500+ platforms; guests get previews and signed-in free accounts have daily limits. Paid Extended scans have a separate scope. Challenges or rate limits can leave a check unknown, and a failed request is not proof the profile was deleted.

cta.label: Search a public username with MyRecon

faq.question: How do I search only personal accounts?
faq.answer: Add type:user in GitHub user search. Use type:org for organizations and user:HANDLE for a known username.

faq.question: Does hiding my profile email hide old commit emails?
faq.answer: No. Profile and commit email exposure are separate. Review your public commits and future commit settings.

faq.question: Does MyRecon inspect private repositories?
faq.answer: No. The public username check does not access private repositories or perform repository secret scanning.

platform.name: GitHub
platform.public_lookup: The checked-in MyRecon standard catalogue lists GitHub. This is a username-level check, not a guarantee that every request will resolve: service changes, rate limits, privacy controls, or temporary blocks can leave a result unknown.
platform.limitations: Coverage depends on the current GitHub interface and supported public checks. Private settings, authentication, rate limits, or technical failures can prevent verification; a missing result is not proof of absence.
platform.privacy_overview: A public GitHub profile can show only the fields its owner and the service make visible, such as a chosen name, image, biography, posts, or outbound links. Private areas and access-controlled content are outside a public lookup.
platform.false_positive_note: A reused or renamed handle, a similarly named profile, a redirect, or a stale search snippet can create a false lead on GitHub. Open the official destination and compare independent public context before attributing it to anyone.

manual_steps: Open github.com/HANDLE or GitHub user search with user:HANDLE.
Confirm the resolved account type and current handle before reviewing repositories.
For your own account, review profile email and commit email settings separately.
method: The signed-out octocat page was opened and captured for this release. Other examples are illustrative and search syntax is attributed to GitHub documentation. Private-account settings and email-change flows were not exercised.
